name: Regression Scan
description: Greps test directories for references to SWE-modified classes and methods so the user knows which tests need re-running before a PR.

testRoots.label: Test Roots
testRoots.description: Comma-separated list of directory names that hold tests in this project. The scan walks these directories (relative to the repo root or any sub-tree) and greps for references to symbols changed in this session. Defaults cover the common conventions across JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and .NET projects. Tighten the list to speed up large repos or add project-specific roots.

fileExtensions.label: File Extensions
fileExtensions.description: Comma-separated list of file extensions the scan will inspect inside the test roots. Each entry includes the leading dot. Limit this when your test files use only one or two extensions to avoid spurious matches in fixture data or generated files.

scanSignals.label: Scan Signals
scanSignals.description: Comma-separated list of symbol categories the scan looks for. classes catches class names from added/modified class definitions. methods catches method names within those classes. exported-functions catches top-level exported functions. public-types catches exported interfaces or type aliases. The agent chooses which extraction patterns to use based on what is enabled here; disabling categories reduces noise on projects with conventions that make a category irrelevant.

runMode.label: Run Mode
runMode.description: Controls how findings are presented. summary groups all matches into a single table by source file, useful for fast triage. perSymbol walks each modified symbol one at a time and lists every test file that references it, useful when you want to investigate one suspected breakage in depth. Both modes use the same underlying grep results; only the presentation differs.

autoOfferOnSignal.label: Auto-Offer On Signal
autoOfferOnSignal.description: When on, TPM proactively offers to run the regression scan after the pre-PR checklist completes, or when the user signals PR readiness without running the checklist. When off, TPM only runs the scan when the user explicitly asks. On is the typical flow where the scan is the third gesture after the checklist and description.

flagThreshold.label: Flag Threshold
flagThreshold.description: Minimum number of test references a modified symbol must have for the scan to flag it as worth attention. Default 1 surfaces every match. Raise it to filter out symbols with only incidental references in fixture data (e.g., set to 2 for projects where most names appear in at least one boilerplate file).
